new_statements.quote: The tones of Lamu appear to be six, exactly as in Lisu: high level [55], rising [35], mid level [33], mid level creaky [33] (Lisu [44], often creaky), low falling [21] and low falling creaky [21]. In the preliminary data presented here, it has not always been possible to distinguish clearly between creaky and non-creaky tones. The frequency of [35] tone in Lamu is much lower than in Lisu; the main correspondence is Lisu [35] to Lamu [55]. [...] The result is that Lamu [55] is a very frequent tone, while Lisu [55] is much less so.

new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (no catalog record, no stress statement held by the project). This is the only first-hand linguistic description of Lamu; it establishes Lamu as tonal (six tones, Lisu-like) and is silent on word stress, so the language's entry can at most be coded 'tone language, no stress statement in the sole source'. Consistent with the ISO 639-3 CR 2007-091 note already read ('a much higher occurrence of high-level tones (Bradley 2004)').
new_statements.rule_in_words: Lamu is a lexical-tone language with (apparently) six tones, the same inventory as Lisu (55, 35, 33, 33 creaky, 21, 21 creaky), with [55] much more frequent than in Lisu; the paper describes segments, clusters, tones, tone correspondences (Table 6) and basic syntax but makes no statement at all about word stress, accent or prominence.
new_statements.exceptions: none concerning stress; on tone: creaky vs non-creaky tones not always distinguishable in the preliminary data; Lamu [55] also reflects some *Low Stopped and all *High Stopped tones.
new_statements.identity_note: Lamu (autonym-based name; Chinese 拉姆/拉莫, classified within the Lahu nationality) of Zhongying township, northeastern Binchuan County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan; Bradley treats it as a Central Ngwi language closest to Lisu (segments, clusters and tone inventory 'almost exactly the same system as in Lisu'), ca. 120 speakers. Data are Bradley's own preliminary field data (wordlist in the appendix alongside Binchuan Lipo, Binchuan Lolo, Lisu and Lahu).
